subject: Horizon AI pricing: hosted per-token commit tiers and model-differentiated premiums
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@horizon.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted per-token commit tiers + model premiums — initial proposal

Hi Priya,

Great speaking earlier — thanks for the context on Horizon's expected mix (chat + retrieval + embeddings) and the seasonal peak in Q1. Attached is an initial pricing sheet that aligns with the usage profile you shared. High-level notes: 

- Base hosted rate (standard chat models): $0.0009 per input token / $0.0014 per output token at the 1M–5M monthly commit slab.
- Commit tiers: 1M–5M, 5M–50M, 50M+ tokens per month. Each step increases the commit discount (sheet has exact slab breakpoints).
- Model-specific premiums: premium/chat-optimized models (we label as "Premium-1" and "Premium-2") carry a multiplier to the base token rate (examples in the sheet are 1.8x and 2.6x respectively).
- Embeddings: priced separately by vector-unit. Example: $0.0012 per 1K embedding requests for standard embedding, with a smaller multiplier for high-dim models.

Two clarifications you asked for: stacking and effective blended rates. In the attached sheet I demonstrate how a commit discount applies to the base rate first, then the model premium multiplier is applied to that discounted base. I also included worked examples for a 10M token/month profile with 60% chat (standard), 30% chat (premium), and 10% embeddings.

Ask: Can you confirm the expected monthly token range (low/typical/peak) and the target contract length (12/24 months)? With those I can produce a revised slab that shows effective per-token costs and a proposed mutual action plan (MAP).

I attached: HorizonAI_Initial_Pricing_Sheet.xlsx (summary + worked examples).

If useful, I can present this to your procurement team next week — Friday morning PT works for me.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Hosted per-token commit tiers + model premiums — initial proposal

Aditya —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the spreadsheet. A few follow-ups from procurement and engineering after reviewing: 

1) Stacking rules: Your example shows commit discount then premium multiplier. Can you confirm whether we can instead apply model premiums to list and then cap the blended effective rate (we'd prefer a blended floor). Is that supported for enterprise commits?

2) Embeddings pricing: we have heavy embedding usage at scale (90M vectors/month for retrieval). Need a clearer unit definition — do you bill per vector generation or per 1K vectors? Also: are there different buckets for production vs. training embeddings?

3) Overage / rollover behavior: If we commit to a monthly token amount and overshoot in a month, how is overage priced? Do unused committed tokens roll over within the contract quarter?

4) Security / compliance: please attach our SOC2 + data residency notes so our InfoSec can validate. Also need a short description of how logs/kv cache retention is handled for hosted customers.

5) Commercial ask: Horizon is evaluating a 12–18 month agreement. Can you provide a sample 12-month MAP with milestones (security review, POC, go-live, DP sync) and a draft MSA + SOW timeline?

We'd like to schedule a 30-min sync on Thurs 12/4 or Fri 12/5 PT to walk the revised math and procurement terms.

Attached: Horizon_RFP_Qs.pdf (procurement questions).

Thanks — Priya
VP Product, Horizon AI
priya@horizon.ai

Subject: Fwd: Horizon procurement questions — negotiation approach

Aditya — quick internal note before our sync. 

Summary of position: Horizon has large embedding volume and a mixed chat footprint with appetite for a 12–18 month term. Procurement will push for a blended floor and a simple overage rate. Our constraints: premium models and high-dim embeddings materially raise cost on our side (GPU + memory), so unrestricted stacking could hurt unit economics. 

Suggested approach: 
- Offer commit discount on base rate, then apply model premium multiplier; however, propose a capped blended floor for the entire usage profile (e.g., not below 60% of list). This addresses their ask for a blended floor while protecting margin.
- For embeddings: offer per-1K vectors pricing with a progressive discount above 50M vectors/mo. Keep a separate premium for high-dim (>=1536).
- Rollover: allow limited rollover up to 10% of monthly commit usable within the quarter; overages billed at a negotiated overage rate that steps down if they exceed a secondary threshold.

Tactical asks for the call: can you produce a worked MAP and 2 pricing scenarios (standard: our baseline multipliers; aggressive: one-time concession to reach commit at 24 months)? I'll join the call and handle procurement asks; Vivek to weigh in on the MAP timeline.

-Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Subject: Revised: Horizon AI hosted pricing + MAP (worked examples)

Priya —

Thanks again — attached is a revised pricing workbook and a short mutual action plan (MAP) that follows the timeline you requested. Key points and explicit worked examples so procurement can see the effective per-token math: 

1) Commit tiers and example effective rates (chat tokens):
   - 1M–5M/mo: base list $0.0009 input / $0.0014 output. 10% commit discount => $0.00081 / $0.00126 effective.
   - 5M–50M/mo: base list discounted to effective $0.00065 / $0.0010 (after slab discount).
   - 50M+/mo: negotiated tier at $0.00045 / $0.00075 (subject to term).

2) Model premiums (applied after slab discount unless otherwise requested):
   - Standard chat: 1.0x
   - Premium-1 (optimsized accuracy/latency mix): 1.7x
   - Premium-2 (state-of-the-art large): 2.5x

   Example: For a 10M token month where 70% is standard chat and 30% is Premium-1, we apply the 5M–50M slab rates to the base, then multiply those base rates for the 30% Premium-1 portion by 1.7 to get the effective premium component. The attached workbook shows the blended per-token effective rate = $0.00078 per token in that example.

3) Embeddings: clarified unit and large-volume buckets:
   - Billing unit: per 1K vectors generated.
   - Standard embedding (<=1024 dim): $0.0012 per 1K vectors at low slab; 25% discount at 50M+/mo.
   - High-dim embedding (>=1536 dim): 1.6x multiplier to standard embedding rate.

4) Rollover and overage:
   - Rollover: up to 10% of unused committed tokens can roll within the same quarter.
   - Overage: billed at the next-higher slab rate with a cap — for the first two overage months we can offer an overage discount of 15% off list overage rates if Horizon commits to a quarterly true-up.

5) Blended floor option (commercial concession):
   - We can offer a capped-blended floor for the first 12 months (subject to term and commit size). Example: floor not to fall below 60% of list effective for the blended profile calculated in the workbook. This is how we can honor a blended-style ask without fully unhooking model premiums from economics.

Security/compliance: attached SOC 2 attestation summary and a short note on logs/kv-cache retention (we retain request-level logs for 90 days by default in hosted; extended retention available as an add-on).

Attachments: HorizonAI_Revised_Pricing_and_MAP.xlsx (pricing workbook + MAP), SOC2_Summary.pdf
